proof.surface: The committed bundles run as Claude Code runs them, including the new dist/session-title-hook.js, against a real nats-server with JetStream and an Envoy listener built from this tree, read back through the listener's GET /v1/sessions.

proof.criterion: The new standalone UserPromptSubmit hook keeps the silent-stdout, always-exit-0 contract with a hand-written payload check in place of zod (reviewer finding 2), and its title file stays inside the state directory (finding 6).
proof.surface: The committed packages/claude-envoy/dist/session-title-hook.js (5,369 bytes), run with Claude Code's hook environment and a payload on stdin.
proof.command: a tester probe running the bundle over nineteen payloads, then ls of the titles directory
proof.observed: Every one exited 0 with an empty stdout: malformed JSON, empty stdin, a JSON array, a bare string, a number, null, a missing session_id, an empty session_id, a numeric session_id, and a null, numeric or object session_title, each with one stderr line naming the field. A good name was recorded, a blank one removed the record, and a 100,000-character name was written whole. A session id of '.' wrote titles/..txt and '..' wrote titles/...txt, both inside the directory, which is what the .txt suffix buys; '../../../../tmp/pwn2' wrote titles/..%2F..%2F..%2F..%2Ftmp%2Fpwn2.txt and created no /tmp/pwn2.
proof.negativeControl: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA unset: exit 0, nothing on stdout, nothing on stderr. A read-only titles directory: exit 0, nothing on stdout, one stderr line 'envoy: could not record the session title — EACCES: permission denied'.

proof.criterion: One pruneStateDirectory serves all three state directories with liveness and age as its predicates, including the role files that were never pruned (the fast-follow the architect asked for in this round).
proof.surface: A live channel server started against a real listener with a state directory seeded by hand.
proof.command: a tester probe seeding roles/old.json and roles/fresh.json, a 31-day-old and a fresh title, sessions/999999 (a dead pid), sessions/<live pid> and sessions/not-a-pid, then starting the committed dist/envoy-channel.js
proof.observed: After one startup: roles/old.json gone, roles/fresh.json present, the 31-day-old title gone, the fresh title present, sessions/999999 gone, the live pid's directory present, and sessions/not-a-pid present — the regex guard keeping a directory whose name is not a number.
proof.negativeControl: The fresh entries in the same sweep: a run that deleted everything, or nothing, would show the same list for both.

startupSweepAttack.why: The architect asked for this one explicitly: reviewer finding 3's goal is that an unreadable state directory must never stop the channel server from starting.
startupSweepAttack.method: chmod 000 on one state directory at a time, the committed dist/envoy-channel.js against main@origin's bundle as the control, both with a real nats-server and listener.
startupSweepAttack.sessionsDirectory: Fixed by this change. main@origin exits: 'Claude Envoy channel server failed: EACCES: permission denied, scandir "<state>/pd/sessions"'. This head stays up and writes one line: 'envoy-channel: could not prune stale session state (EACCES: permission denied, scandir "<state>/pd/sessions")'. Its heartbeat then reports 'registry heartbeat failed (EACCES ... open "<state>/pd/sessions/<pid>/session-id"); retrying every heartbeat' each beat, so the session stays registered under the name it started with while that directory cannot be read.
startupSweepAttack.rolesDirectory: Not fixed, and identical on both bundles: 'Claude Envoy channel server failed: EACCES: permission denied, open "<state>/pd/roles/<session id>.json"', the process exits, and the Agents page keeps a row that never beats again. The cause is not a sweep: restoreRole runs in the serialized block at packages/claude-envoy/src/envoy-channel-server.ts:804-807, above the best-effort prune loop, and readPersistedRole tolerates a missing file but not an unreadable one. Pre-existing — the control proves it — so it is not a failure of this round, and the architect has decided (Envoy, 2026-10-25T04:11:36Z) that the two-line fix lands in this pull request rather than as a separate issue.
startupSweepAttack.healthyDirectories: The sweep results in the fourth proof entry above.

hookCost.note: Three runs each, same loop, same machine, under this pod's load. The reviewer's ~115 ms of overhead is gone; about 25 ms over bare Bun remains, which the implement handoff calls 'nothing measurable'.
